title: Would these line segments meet if we extended them?
description: Two pairs of line segments are drawn. One pair leans a little towards each other and the other keeps the same gap along its length. The board extends each pair in the mind and says which pair is likely to meet. Keeko doubts that a small lean never meets.
teaching_notes: One idea: a gap that closes, however slowly, ends in a meeting, and a gap that stays the same never closes. Watch for students who think a very small lean means the lines never meet.

source: Two more pairs are drawn: ST and UV lean towards each other by about 2.5° and look nearly side by side; OP and QR keep about the same gap along their whole length. Are ST and UV likely to meet if extended? Are OP and QR?
video_script.why: The child decides by looking at the gap whether two segments would meet if they were extended.
video_script.substitution: The book's own question about two pairs of line segments: is each pair likely to meet if it is extended, decided by what happens to the gap between the segments.
video_script.anchor: Two pairs of line segments: S T and U V leaning a little towards each other, and O P and Q R keeping the same gap along their whole length.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a lean as small as two point five degrees can never close the gap.
video_script.payoff_line: S T and U V would meet if extended far enough. O P and Q R are not likely to meet.

final_answer.value: ST and UV would meet if extended far enough; OP and QR are not likely to meet
final_answer.spoken: S T and U V would meet if extended far enough, and O P and Q R are not likely to meet

hold_back: ST and UV would meet if extended far enough; OP and QR are not likely to meet
maths_rules: ST and UV lean towards each other by about 2.5, so the gap between them gets smaller
a gap that keeps getting smaller closes, so ST and UV would meet far beyond T and V
OP and QR keep the same gap from one end to the other, so the gap does not close
for lines this close, a judgement by eye is only a guess, and a sure test is needed
the slip: 2.5 is small, but any lean closes the gap if the lines are extended far enough
video_script.design: The two pairs stay on the stage. Each pair is drawn longer past its ends, and the gap between the segments is marked at both ends to show whether it closes.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>If the gap closes, the segments will meet. If it stays the same, they will not.
